drafts.walkScript: Turn to the mark at the very end. The sentence opens with “Did”, so it asks something. An asking sentence needs a question mark, not a full stop. The commas mark a pair and a list.

Look at the second part, after “Once the rain stopped”. “The doors” runs straight into “the class”, with a whole sentence on each side. They need a full stop, or a comma and “and”. The other three parts hold.
Read the sentence to its very end. A sentence that tells something closes with a full stop. Here, after “office”, there is no mark at all. The earlier commas hold.

Check each mark in turn. The question mark after “this” sits inside the speech marks. The comma after “Mrs Okonjo” leads into the part about the kit. The mark in “boys’” sits after the s, which fits more than one boy. The full stop after “gate” closes the sentence, so No mistake fits.
